items.headline: Brent +1.2% to $110.11 on the Saudi ordered departure; State Dept walks back Gulf-wide report; explosions reported near Sirik, Iran
bullets: Oil caught a bid in Thursday Asia trade on the Saudi ordered departure: Brent futures +1.2% to $110.11, WTI +1% to $98.12 (Reuters, Oct 22).

State Dept spokesman Pigott called the earlier media report of Gulf-wide departures 'inaccurate' -- the order covers Saudi Arabia only; other missions' family withdrawals (per 4 US officials) still unconfirmed by State.

Iranian media reported explosions near Sirik in southern Iran on Wednesday, nature and origin unknown (via Reuters); Kpler counts at least 18 attacks on shipping in the past two weeks. FX sat it out: DXY 101.70 flat, EUR/USD 1.1230, USD/JPY 158.10 -- noise.

items.headline: NYT: US/Israel drew up post-midterm Iran strike plans; Houthi strikes kill at Dammam airport and Shaybah oilfield
bullets: The New York Times (reported Wednesday, via multiple relays): US and Israeli militaries have drawn up specific plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms -- targets include nuclear sites, missile/drone arsenal and energy infrastructure; Hegseth met Netanyahu in Israel this week; the buildup including three carriers is expected to be in place by early November. Trump has not approved and has vetoed similar plans repeatedly this year.

After the ordered departure: Saudi energy ministry said debris from the interception of a drone targeting Aramco's Shaybah oilfield killed 2 (a Filipino and a Nepali) and injured 2; Reuters also reports a Houthi attack on Dammam's King Fahd airport killed 1 and injured 8.

Iran's FM Araghchi: Tehran will give diplomacy 'another chance' if it sees 'strong evidence of a sincere desire' from the US -- but if the US chooses war, 'it'll certainly result in an even greater strategic failure.' FX still quiet: USD/JPY ~158.1, DXY ~101.7, Brent $109.92 -- no repricing, so Flash only, no chat ping.

items.headline: US issues ordered departure for non-essential staff and families in Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
bullets: State Dept spokesman Tommy Pigott announced an ordered departure of non-emergency US government employees and their families in Saudi Arabia; other Gulf missions are also trimming staff (Reuters, CNN, Oct 21).
The Riyadh embassy warned US citizens of possible further Houthi attacks on Saudi airports after recent deadly strikes on King Khalid airport, oil infrastructure and shipping.
Escalation confirmed, but FX is still quiet: USD/JPY holding the lower-158 range in Asia, DXY steady — oil is the transmission channel to watch overnight.

items.headline: US Treasury sanctions Karnakis & Karnakis law firm + Iran shadow-fleet network (Operation Economic Outcast)
bullets: OFAC designated Greece/Panama law firm Karnakis & Karnakis, 5 individuals, Singapore- and UAE-based shipping agents, and blocked 9 vessels under EO 13902 — accused of concealing Iranian oil, petrochemical and steel shipments (Treasury, Oct 21).
FinCEN issued its first-ever admin subpoena under 31 USC 5318(k) probing a Greek bank's Iran ties, plus info requests to six other European banks over Iran-linked relationships.
Still the enforcement lane, not the strike lane: Reuters notes Washington has 'held off striking Iran this month' and is running the blockade + sanction waves instead — oil price reaction nil so far.
